title: Article: How a mantra gets jagrit?

segments.text: A mantra becomes jagrit (awakened) when it is chanted a specific number of times, allowing it to take form as a mantra doot (mantra energy messenger).

For example, if a person consistently chants a mantra with full dedication, the energy of that mantra gradually builds up. After reaching a certain number of repetitions—let’s say a few million times—the mantra awakens and starts working on its own. At this stage, the mantra not only strengthens the person’s spiritual connection but also acts as a guide and protector, assisting him in his spiritual journey.
Does energizing a mantra is related to Sankalp shakti of a person?

In the first dimension , a mantra moves either forward or backward when chanted. As an aspirant continues his practice, the mantra gains more movement—it can go forward, backward, upward, downward, left, and right. At this stage, the mantra also develops the ability to heal others.

For example, imagine an aspirant who begins chanting a mantra. At first, the mantra only moves in one direction. But with consistent practice, they start noticing that the mantra’s energy expands in different ways, allowing them to use it for healing and protection.
In the fourth dimension , the mantra moves both downward and upward, enabling the aspirant’s astral body to work in multiple places at the same time.

Finally, in the seventh dimension , the mantra becomes even more powerful. It can now travel beyond the physical and astral realms, reaching different loks (spiritual worlds), allowing the aspirant to connect with higher divine energies
How to keep the mantra energized forever?
To keep a mantra energized, it needs a continuous flow of universal energy. This energy is created only through the constant chanting of that mantra.

For example, think of a light bulb connected to a battery. As long as the battery is being charged, the bulb stays lit. But if you stop charging the battery, it slowly loses power, and the light dims or goes out.
Similarly, if someone stops chanting the mantra, the energy that keeps it powerful stops being generated. As a result, the mantra loses its strength and won’t work as effectively as before.
